products.short_description: A branch-based diagnostic runbook and 5 read-only PowerShell scripts for blocked or failing calls to the Microsoft Graph Copilot admin (beta) endpoints — /beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages and friends. Decode 401/403/404/429 into one named cause: missing scope, missing admin role, app-only-vs-delegated, ungranted consent, preview not flighted, cloud not enabled, license, wrong path, throttling, or a genuine limitation — each with the fix or the supported fallback. Verified against Microsoft Learn; beta-volatile facts flagged.
products.description:
Turn an ambiguous Copilot admin 403 into one named cause — and unblock it

You called a Microsoft Graph Copilot admin (beta) endpoint — most likely GET /beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id} to read the agent catalog — and it came back blocked. The body says “Access is denied to the requested resource,” or “User context is required,” or a bare 404, and the preview docs will not tell you which of a dozen unrelated things is actually wrong. So the team burns hours guessing between a missing permission, a missing admin role, an app-token-vs-user-token problem, an ungranted consent, a preview that has not reached your tenant, a cloud where the feature does not exist, a license prerequisite, a wrong path, throttling, or a capability that simply is not there yet.

This runbook ends the guessing. It is a branch-based diagnostic method for the entire /beta/copilot/admin/* surface: a Step-0 fact-finding pass, then Branches A–J that route your exact HTTP status and error text to one root cause — each with how to confirm it, the fix or supported workaround, and how to re-validate. It is broader than any single report or export: it is about making any Graph Copilot admin request work, proving whether the data is truly exposed, and — where beta cannot be relied on — routing you to the supported path that can.

Run it yourself — simpler, cheaper, and proven

You do not need a consultant or a Microsoft premier ticket to start. The package hands you the field-tested method as self-guided, click-by-click documentation a competent admin or developer can follow end to end — backed by five read-only PowerShell scripts.

  • Simpler — exact, ordered steps; the 401-vs-403 and scope-vs-role distinctions made concrete; every artifact you create (the CPADMDX-Diagnostics folder, the CPADMDX-Findings.json evidence file) named and reused through testing and troubleshooting.
  • Cheaper — one fixed price instead of an open consulting meter (comparable work runs ~$1,500–$3,000/day). Reusable on the next preview-API investigation you hit.
  • Tested — a pilot-first method (Assess → Configure → Pilot → Validate → Expand) with five PASS/FAIL gates that prove the call now works and whether the data is actually exposed.

What's inside

  • Solution Overview — what the /beta/copilot/admin/* surface is (package catalog, policy settings, usage reports), Microsoft's GA-vs-beta support posture, and the diagnostic model built on 401-vs-403 and scope-vs-role.
  • Requirements Guide — the nine prerequisites to call the endpoints (tooling, a delegated admin, the exact scopes CopilotPackages.Read.All / CopilotPolicySettings.Read, the AI Administrator role, admin consent, the correct cloud, licensing, tenant flighting, the evidence file), each with how to verify and implement-if-missing.
  • Diagnostic Runbook — Step 0 fact-finding plus ten branches (A–J): 401 auth; app-only “user context required”; missing scope; ungranted consent; missing admin role; cloud not enabled (Global-only — GCC High/DoD excluded); license prerequisite (Agent 365 — acknowledged and excluded per your finding); wrong path/version; throttling; and genuine product limitation — each symptom → confirm → fix/workaround → re-validate.
  • 5 read-only PowerShell scripts (Microsoft Graph, GET-only, cloud switch -Environment Global|USGov|USGovDoD): a preflight that reports your delegated-vs-app status, token scopes and admin roles; an endpoint probe that decodes the real 401/403/404/429 into a branch; a have-vs-need scope/role resolver; a supported-fallback tester (GA usage reports, GA catalog, admin-center/Purview pointers); and a findings consolidator. They never fabricate a beta response — if the call fails, they report the real error.
  • Testing & Troubleshooting Guides with five pass/fail gates and the preview-specific traps (throttling storms, tenant-not-enabled flighting, undocumented-endpoint deprecation), plus Best Practices on when to depend on beta vs wait for GA.

Accuracy you can trust on a moving target

Every endpoint path, permission scope, admin role, license requirement, error meaning, and cloud-availability fact was verified against Microsoft Learn on the build date. Because this is a preview surface that changes without notice, every volatile claim is flagged “verify against current Microsoft documentation.” Where the honest answer is “the data is not exposed” or “do not depend on this,” the runbook says so and points you to the supported path — it never invents an endpoint, scope, or response shape.

The repeatable way

Every solution follows the same repeatable shape, so each investigation feels familiar and low-risk — buy once, reuse the method for the next preview-API or Copilot-admin problem.

The bottom line

A blocked Graph Copilot admin call turned into a single named cause and fixed — or, where beta cannot be relied on, a proven, supported alternative delivering the data you need — with a repeatable method and scripts you keep and reuse.

What you receive — every file in your download

This package is delivered as a single ZIP you keep and reuse across unlimited investigations — nothing is left out and nothing else is required:

  • Implementation Guide (PDF & Word) — the complete, click-by-click runbook: overview, requirements, the ten-branch diagnostic tree, testing & validation, troubleshooting, and best practices.
  • PowerShell Scripts (ZIP) — 5 ready-to-run read-only scripts (all cloud-aware, GET-only):
    • CPADMDX-Preflight.ps1 — report the signed-in account, delegated-vs-app-only, token scopes, directory roles, and cloud
    • CPADMDX-Probe-Endpoint.ps1 — call the target endpoint and decode the real 401/403/404/429 into the likely branch
    • CPADMDX-Resolve-Scopes.ps1 — report have-vs-need for scopes and admin role, isolating a scope gap from a role gap
    • CPADMDX-Test-Fallbacks.ps1 — exercise the supported alternatives (GA usage reports, GA catalog, admin-center/Purview pointers)
    • CPADMDX-Report-Findings.ps1 — consolidate everything into CPADMDX-Diagnostics\CPADMDX-Findings.json for your support case

Delivered as a Word document and PDF, plus all PowerShell scripts, in a single ZIP — yours to keep and reuse.
